rules.sentence: Clinical features mimic those of esophageal cancer, with progressive dysphagia as a common characteristic.
Nodular and ulcerative lesions are typical findings.
Biopsied lesions typically show caseating and noncaseating granulomas.
Acid-fast staining, PCR, and culture of biopsied tissues should be performed.[19]
Anorexia, weight loss, and gastric outlet obstruction are common clinical manifestations.
Additionally, ulcerative and hypertrophic lesions can be seen by endoscopy.
Pyloric stenosis may develop in the late stage of the disease.
Lymphadenopathy can result in extrinsic compression of the duodenum.[15][8]
